races.name: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Rory Rocket
runners_data.note: Three wins at six furlongs on Good ground in recent form is a compelling profile fit here; Gary & Josh Moore yard in decent nick at T14 and Jude Fernandes rides, hold-up style that may need to work harder than ideal given the likely sedate tempo but course-and-distance record is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Headgear noted (p) and handles Good ground as the sim-going record shows; Matthew Slater takes the ride for James Bennett whose T14 is a blank, and the five-year-old has placed form over six furlongs here but is another pure closer who needs the pace to stack up for maximum effect.

runners_data.name: Calafrio
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who sets the tactical table for this entire race; 189 days off and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 tempers confidence, but if they recreate their six-furlong Sandown win they will be very hard to pass with a clear lead and a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm.

runners_data.name: Lahina Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Rachel Cook & John Bridger who drops into a small field and is likely to inherit the position closest to Calafrio; placed four times in the last five over six furlongs suggests consistency without a killer punch, but tactical position here may prove an asset.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's four-year-old has placed form over this trip and wears a hood (p); in truth a genuine hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects that this field is too compressed at the rear, so their actual on-track position could end up closer to the pace than usual — the STYLE_FIT tag appropriately dims the win expectation.

runners_data.name: Snooker Mccrew
runners_data.note: 683 days off the track is the headline flag — this is Snooker Mccrew's first run since a July 2023 win over a mile at Sandown, a very different trip and going combination to today's six furlongs on Good to Firm; a true hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map due to overcrowding at the rear, Max Comley sends them out fit or otherwise but caution is strongly warranted on comeback.

races.paceDynamic: Calafrio is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field on Good to Firm ground at Salisbury, and with no genuine rival to press them early, they are set to control the tempo at a sustainable rather than scorching clip over six furlongs. Lahina Bay will likely slot in just behind from a prominent pitch, giving the race a clean, processional shape from the gates. The pace dynamic strongly favours horses who can track the leader within a length or two and kick off the turn, rather than deep hold-up types who need a true gallop to close into. Rory Rocket and Dark Sun are the natural closers, but with the pace unlikely to be fierce, their finishing kicks may arrive too late against a front-runner who is never seriously tested — this shape leans unmistakably in favour of prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can sit close and pounce, not pure hold-up horses waiting for a collapse that may not come. Be An Angel and Snooker Mccrew are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more closers than can all find a natural rear position; neither is likely to secure their preferred deep berth, but their actual running position may end up more prominent than their style profile suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Calafrio Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Calafrio is allowed to stride clear and dictate an unchallenged, even tempo throughout with no rival willing to go with them.
scenarios.body: Calafrio settles into a rhythm on the front end and, never put under pressure, simply finds enough from their prominent perch to repel challengers who have had to make ground from further back on ground that rewards pace. Lahina Bay, sitting closest in the slipstream, is best placed to pounce if Calafrio flattens out, while Rory Rocket's strong recent form at this trip and going gives them an each-way claim tracking into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a runner sits close enough to Calafrio through the first four furlongs and produces a decisive surge off the home turn.
scenarios.body: Rory Rocket, who has won twice over this exact course-and-distance combination on Good ground, is ideally placed to exploit a sustained gallop by covering the leader early and running them down in the final furlong. Dark Sun has similar profile credentials and recent winning form over five to six furlongs on Good, making either a plausible beneficiary if the front-runner's advantage erodes.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Snatch It
scenarios.trigger: If Calafrio sets a fast enough clip to tie up the prominently-placed runners and the hold-up horses find a late surge.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a pace that the current race shape — one uncontested front-runner on Good to Firm — is unlikely to generate, making it a low-probability outcome. Be An Angel and Snooker Mccrew are the beneficiaries in theory, but both are tagged as redistributed true hold-up types who may not even secure deep enough positions to produce a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Contested Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Lahina Bay or another runner pushes up to challenge Calafrio early and a brief battle for the lead causes the tempo to spike.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace over this distance on fast ground would scramble the race shape and potentially leave the front two vulnerable, opening the door for a hold-up or midfield horse to scoop the spoils late. However this scenario is inherently unlikely given Calafrio's confirmed front-running role and Lahina Bay's tendency to settle in second rather than force the issue.

watchPoints.text: Snooker Mccrew returns after 683 days absent and drops sharply in trip from a mile to six furlongs — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness or early panic in the market that could inflate their odds falsely.

Calafrio's 189-day layoff means their fitness for a flat-out six-furlong blast on Good to Firm is unproven; if they fade sharply inside the final furlong, the entire race shape collapses and Lahina Bay rather than a hold-up horse profits most.

Be An Angel and Snooker Mccrew as genuine deep closers may end up racing closer to the pace than usual given the compressed field — watch whether they settle or get caught up in an unnatural position early, which would undermine their chance of a late run.

Rory Rocket's recent form reads 1-1-6-1-0-0 across the last six — the two blanks bookend a hat-trick of wins and this going and trip combination at Salisbury has previously suited them well; watch whether Jude Fernandes elects to track Calafrio or drops in behind the group.

races.name: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Richard 'Dick' Robathan Memorial Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Gloryous
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up filly whose best recent effort was a second over 10f on Good, but the uncontested pace set by Oh Yes You Do may not generate enough of a gallop for William Carson to deliver her signature late challenge; 12 days since last run is a positive freshness signal.|

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: Back from an 86-day break for Jack Channon, and while her sole win came over 10f on Good which ticks both boxes, Rose Dawes (5) takes off a useful 5lb and her hold-up style will need a stronger tempo than this shape looks likely to provide.|

runners_data.name: Food For Thought
runners_data.note: An interesting style unknown (U) for Ralph Beckett who runs a high volume of winners; her recent win at 10f on Good is directly relevant, and Hector Crouch can position her wherever suits — if she tracks the leader she is the most versatile threat in the field.|

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly has genuine hold-up tendencies but is mapped to midfield given the density of closers in this field — her most recent run was a second at 9f on Good which shows she acts on the surface, but racing outside her natural rear-of-field comfort zone tempers her chance meaningfully.|

runners_data.name: Oh Yes You Do
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, and David Menuisier's three-year-old has form figures of 1-1 at 8f-10f, making this trip a small question; Joe Leavy can dictate terms unchallenged, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she is doing exactly what she naturally does — the only caveat is whether she gets the trip fully.|

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: William Haggas's filly is lightly raced and has shown little sparkle in three runs, with no wins or places, and while the switch to better going than her soft-ground efforts could theoretically help, she is a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield role she is unlikely to embrace naturally at this stage of her development.|

races.paceDynamic: Oh Yes You Do is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner fillies' handicap over 1m2f at Salisbury, and with no rival likely to press her hard for the lead, she should control proceedings at a comfortable, measured gallop on ground that has been riding Good to Firm throughout the card. That uncontested pace is likely to be sustainable rather than searching, meaning the race will be set up as a test of finishing quality rather than raw stamina, with the front portion of the field in a strong tactical position approaching the straight. Gloryous, Pomme Pomme, Mayaada, and Silver Lake are all natural hold-up types, but the map cannot accommodate four closers at the rear — Mayaada and Silver Lake are redistributed to midfield positions they would not naturally seek, meaning the true late-running contingent is thinner than it first appears. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses with a turn of foot that can sit just off Oh Yes You Do's uncontested lead, then deliver a clean challenge in the final two furlongs without needing a deep, strongly-run pace to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Oh Yes You Do Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Oh Yes You Do leads unopposed and controls the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets a comfortable gallop from the front and, with no rival able to apply pressure, quickens clear when asked in the straight on ground that suits quick finishers over staying types. Front-running or close-tracking profiles benefit enormously here, as the slow-medium pace negates hold-up runners who need a strong gallop to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Oh Yes You Do within a length and outkicks her from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The controlled gallop allows a well-positioned tracker to conserve energy and then produce a sharper turn of foot than the leader in the closing stages. Food For Thought's style and course-appropriate form makes her the most obvious beneficiary if she settles close to the pace and quickens past.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the closers get a genuine gallop to chase.
scenarios.body: A faster tempo would stretch the field and give genuine hold-up horses like Gloryous and Pomme Pomme the moving target they need to close on, though with only one pace-setter this scenario requires an unlikely increase in tempo. Gloryous's best form has come when there is something to chase, and Pomme Pomme's win at 1m2f on Good suggests she stays well enough to be finishing strongly at the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Drift Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If interference or a stumbled start disrupts the field and bunches the race mid-run.
scenarios.body: A stop-start rhythm would compress the field and bring hold-up types like Mayaada and Silver Lake into contention earlier than their natural style demands, though both are mapped out of role and face a significant ask to win racing against type. This is the least likely shape given the small field and clean early configuration, but Mayaada's recent second at 9f on Good hints at residual ability if the race falls her way.

watchPoints.text: Oh Yes You Do must be monitored for whether Joe Leavy allows a genuinely slow or suspiciously dawdling gallop — if the pace is artificially slow, even modest hold-up horses can close, flipping the race shape entirely.
Pomme Pomme returns from 86 days off for Jack Channon — watch market moves at the off, as fitness on seasonal reappearance is unproven and could see her drop away if the race is run at any real pace.

Food For Thought's style is listed as unknown — watch how Hector Crouch positions her in the early furlongs, as she could track Oh Yes You Do in second and become the primary threat, or drift back into the hold-up pack and lose her tactical advantage.

Silver Lake is lightly raced with only three career starts and no placed efforts — if she shows greenness or is slowly away under Darragh Keenan, the field's already compressed shape could cause crowding for those behind her in the straight.

races.name: Redbrook Clinic Handicap

runners_data.name: Zipwire
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by J S Moore, 26 days fresh, has been creeping up the form ladder with a recent win over the trip at Stamford; quick ground on turf brings no concern but her sim-going record at 1m2f shows no wins or places in four attempts, so she needs the pace to collapse.|

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Athene
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly returns after a lengthy 206-day absence, which is the single biggest concern; she has shown front-running form at 8f on Stamford turf and now steps up in trip, and while she is the natural pace-setter, her fitness after seven months off and the style-fit flag (STYLE_FIT=0.90) temper confidence at this distance.|

runners_data.name: Three Socks On
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's progressive three-year-old comes into this on the back of back-to-back wins and is proven over 10f, and apprentice Owen Lewis taking 5lb off is a genuine advantage; goes on a range of ground, has placed on Good going, and his prominent style is perfectly aligned with sitting just off an uncontested pace on Good to Firm.|

runners_data.name: Evening Fades
runners_data.note: William Haggas holds a strong hand in terms of trainer reputation, but this hold-up filly has been beaten in all three starts including two over the trip, and her best effort on sim going is just one placing from three; needs something to go wrong for the leaders.|

runners_data.name: Shirakawa
runners_data.note: Winner over 10f on Good last time out for Eve Johnson Houghton, which is her most relevant form angle; she is a true hold-up horse placed into a midfield position on the map because the rear is congested, and her STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that she is unlikely to be racing from her natural position, which limits confidence unless the race falls apart in front of her.|

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Athene is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and, with no rivals likely to press her hard, she should be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 1m2f trip at Salisbury. The hold-up contingent — Zipwire and Evening Fades — will be anchored at the rear with Shirakawa, who is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the field's backend is congested with closers; Three Socks On should slot into a prominent tracking role just behind Spirit Of Athene. With the going riding Good To Firm (all earlier 1m2f races confirmed Good To Firm), the surface will be quick enough that an uncontested leader setting an honest but not punishing pace is unlikely to be reeled in easily. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or pace-tracking profile — horses that can sit within striking range of Spirit Of Athene through the final turn and pounce without needing to make up significant ground on a tight, uncontested pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Athene bowls clear uncontested and sets a measured, comfortable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Athene dictates every yard, the hold-up horses are left with too much to do on the quick ground and the runner-up emerges from the prominent tracking position closest to the pace; Three Socks On, proven over the trip with recent course-distance form, is best placed to latch on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Athene sets a fraction too strong early and ties up in the final furlong, allowing closers to pick her off.
scenarios.body: Zipwire or Evening Fades, tracking from the rear, finds a clear run turning in on the quick ground and finishes off a weakening leader; this is more plausible for Zipwire given her recent stepback win over the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overhauls
scenarios.trigger: If Three Socks On travels powerfully in Spirit Of Athene's slipstream and goes past her approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Three Socks On has won twice recently and her stamina for 1m2f is confirmed; pressing close to an unextended leader on fast ground, she could hit the front and hold on as hold-up horses fail to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shirakawa Runs Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or gaps open wide enough for Shirakawa to thread through from an uncharacteristically forward position.
scenarios.body: Shirakawa has a single win over 10f on Good and is a genuine hold-up type forced into a midfield slot; this scenario requires an unlikely collapse in front combined with a clear passage, making it the lowest-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Of Athene's 206-day absence is a major flag — watch for any early signs she is running green or failing to stride out fluently, which would signal she is short of full fitness and open the race up for Three Socks On.|

Three Socks On's apprentice jockey Owen Lewis must judge the pace correctly and not get caught wide into the final turn; if he tracks Spirit Of Athene cleanly and keeps it tight, his 5lb claim becomes a significant asset.|

Zipwire's hold-up style depends entirely on Spirit Of Athene setting enough of a gallop to come back to the closers — with only five runners and a lone confirmed front-runner, that gallop may simply be too steady for Zipwire to reel in.|

Shirakawa's redistribution to midfield means punters should not be surprised if she actually races further back than shown; watch where Callum Hutchinson positions her in the early stages, as sitting behind a slow pace from the rear will make her task very difficult.|

Going is confirmed Good To Firm for the 1m2f trip at Salisbury across multiple earlier races on the card — no softening expected, which favours horses with proven form on quicker ground and marginally disadvantages Three Socks On's most recent placing on Soft.|

races.name: Taste The World Handicap

runners_data.name: Zen Diva
runners_data.note: Won over C&D last time (good, 6f) and drops into a handicap with Ralph Beckett continuing strong form; the sole front-runner here so secures an uncontested lead, though tagged STYLE_FIT as a prominent rather than natural leader, which slightly tempers confidence in her ability to dominate wire-to-wire at full handicap company.

runners_data.name: The Lost Sock
runners_data.note: Roger Varian hold-up sprinter wearing a hood, 9 days since last run over 6f at Sandown; placed at the trip twice in recent starts and good-ground form is solid across nine runs, though a tendency to race keenly from behind means traffic management in a small field is key.

runners_data.name: Charlie Boyo
runners_data.note: Andrew Cox's gelding carries a tongue-tie and won last time out over this exact C&D trip in good ground — the most relevant recent form in the race; runs as a hold-up type with a 6f Salisbury win already banked, making him the standout profile for a late-run scenario if Zen Diva sets enough pace.

runners_data.name: Remi Mae
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly has been placed twice at 6f on good ground and is a genuine hold-up operator who has been shuffled forward on the pace map only because the field is stacked with closers; at OR 69 she is the lowest-rated runner and would need a very specific pace scenario to land a blow, with the redistribution being context rather than expectation.

races.paceDynamic: Zen Diva is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should bowl along at a sustainable, self-regulated clip from flag to finish on good ground at Salisbury's straight six. The three hold-up types — The Lost Sock, Charlie Boyo, and Remi Mae — will be racing from behind a single, uncontested pace-setter, meaning the tempo Zen Diva sets is entirely in her own hands and unlikely to be pressurising. This field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Remi Mae is a true closer who has been redistributed to a midfield slot because there is simply no room for all three to hunt from deep — Charlie Boyo and The Lost Sock, with stronger recent form and more course-relevant profiles, are better placed to secure the rearward positions naturally. The uncontested lead with a small, manageable field on good ground strongly favours either a wire-to-wire front-runner if Zen Diva can dictate at a moderate tempo, or a single late burst from the most powerful closer if she sets enough gallop to be caught — on balance, the shape marginally favours hold-up horses who can produce one clean run in the straight, provided Zen Diva does not dawdle to a crawl.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zen Diva Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zen Diva dictates a comfortable, uncontested tempo and the closers cannot sustain their finish over the full straight.
scenarios.body: Zen Diva takes the rail position and controls pace entirely through the first half of the six furlongs, arriving at the two-pole with energy in reserve; with no rival having pushed her early, she kicks clear and holds on as the hold-up horses arrive too late or lack the acceleration to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Zen Diva sets a strong enough gallop that the hold-up horses can reel her in with a powerful late run.
scenarios.body: Zen Diva's natural front-running instinct sees her go off briskly, spending more energy than a small field dictates, and the straight six gives the closers the run of the race to pick her off in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle stages and a prominent-to-midfield type outstays the field in a muddling finish.
scenarios.body: Zen Diva slows to a crawl setting no genuine pace, the hold-up horses fail to generate momentum late, and the race becomes a stamina-test rather than a sprint finish; a horse travelling well in transit exploits the resulting slow-burn contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Remi Mae produces an exceptional late thrust from the widest angle and the pace was honest enough throughout.
scenarios.body: Remi Mae, though mapped forward of her natural position, races as a true closer at the back and finds a seam in the straight; she requires everything to fall perfectly and the pace to suit, making this the lowest-probability shape given her redistribution and modest OR of 69.

watchPoints.text: Charlie Boyo's C&D course win last time out in identical conditions (6f, Salisbury, good) makes him the most dangerous closer if Zen Diva sets any meaningful pace — watch for him to be produced wide and late.

Zen Diva's jockey Hector Crouch will face a tactical decision on whether to dictate or conserve — if she is allowed to dawdle in front with no pressure, the closers' runs may come too late and the front-runner steals it.

The Lost Sock's hood is worth monitoring at the start — if he jumps slowly or is caught in traffic behind two other hold-up types, his chance evaporates in a race of only four runners with little room to manoeuvre.

With all three rivals running hold-up styles, Zen Diva may get an even softer lead than normal for a small-field 6f sprint — any sign she is travelling strongly past the halfway point should be treated as a significant danger signal.

Remi Mae's redistribution to midfield is artificial; backers should expect her to drop to the rear early and require a stronger-than-expected pace injection from Zen Diva to have any realistic chance of getting competitive.
